recipes.title: Bife de Chorizo with Chimichurri
recipes.dish_alt: A seared bife de chorizo steak with a dark crust and pink medium-rare center, served with greens
recipes.prep_alt: A jar of fresh green chimichurri sauce being stirred with a spoon

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Bife de chorizo or sirloin strip steak

sections.heading: Steps
items: Take the steak out of the fridge 20 minutes before cooking. Pat dry and season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.

Make the chimichurri: combine the parsley, garlic, oregano, red pepper flakes, vinegar, and water in a bowl. Whisk in the olive oil. Season with salt and let sit at room temperature at least 15 minutes so the flavors meld (it keeps well in the fridge up to a week).
Heat a heavy skillet or grill pan over high heat with the searing oil until just smoking.
Sear the steak 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, adjusting time for thickness and desired doneness, pressing gently for an even crust.
Rest the steak 5 minutes before slicing against the grain.
Spoon chimichurri generously over the steak and serve extra on the side.

recipes.title: Milanesa a la Napolitana
recipes.dish_alt: A breaded Milanesa Napolitana topped with melted mozzarella and sliced tomato, served with french fries
recipes.prep_alt: A Milanesa Napolitana topped with tomato sauce and cheese, plated with a side of french fries

sections.heading: Steps
items: Pound the beef cutlets to an even ½cm thickness between plastic wrap.
Set up a dredging station: flour seasoned with garlic powder, salt, and pepper; beaten egg; breadcrumbs.
Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing to adhere.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the cutlets 2-3 minutes per side until golden and just cooked through. Drain on paper towels.
Preheat the oven broiler (or oven to 220°C/425°F). Arrange the fried cutlets on a baking sheet.
Spread tomato sauce over each cutlet, top with a slice of ham, then mozzarella, then a pinch of oregano.
Broil or bake 5-8 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Serve hot - classically with french fries or a simple salad.

recipes.title: Empanadas de Carne
recipes.dish_alt: A tray of golden-baked Argentine beef empanadas with crimped edges, served with lime wedges
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Crimped and Ready to Bake
recipes.prep_alt: Raw crimped empanadas arranged on a metal tray, ready to go into the oven

sections.heading: Steps
items: Heat a splash of oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 5-7 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the ground beef, breaking it up, and cook until browned.
Stir in the paprika, cumin, oregano, and chili flakes (if using), cooking 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the stock and simmer 5 minutes until moist but not soupy. Season with salt. Spread on a tray and let cool completely - hot filling will melt the dough.
Once cool, stir in the chopped hard-boiled egg and olives.
Lay out the empanada discs. Place a spoonful of filling just off-center on each.
Moisten the edge with a little water or egg wash, fold into a half-moon, and press to seal. Crimp in the traditional repulgue braid, or press with a fork.
Arrange on a lined baking sheet, brush with egg wash, and bake at 200°C/400°F for 18-22 minutes until golden.
Serve warm, with lime wedges if you like.

recipes.title: Locro (Weeknight-Shortcut Version)
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of thick, golden Locro stew with visible corn kernels, beans, and meat
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Locro Simmering in the Pot
recipes.prep_alt: A large pot of golden Locro stew simmering over a wood fire

sections.heading: Steps
items: In a large heavy pot, brown the beef and pork over medium-high heat in a little oil, in batches if needed. Remove and set aside.
Add the chorizo and onion to the same pot, cooking 5 minutes until the onion softens and the chorizo releases some fat.
Stir in the paprika and cumin, cooking 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the beef and pork to the pot. Add the hominy, beans, squash, bay leaf, and stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, partially covered, 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally and mashing some of the squash against the side of the pot, until thick and stew-like and the meat is tender.
Meanwhile, make the salsa criolla: combine the onion, bell pepper, vinegar, oil, and paprika in a small bowl. Let sit at room temperature to marinate.
Season the locro with salt. Serve in deep bowls topped with a spoonful of salsa criolla.

recipes.title: Sorrentinos de Jamón y Queso
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of round stuffed sorrentinos pasta topped with a chunky meat sauce
recipes.prep_alt: Fresh sorrentinos pasta pieces submerged in a pot of boiling water, next to their packaging

sections.heading: Steps
items: Make the dough: mound the flour, make a well, and add the egg(s), olive oil, and salt. Gradually work the flour into the wet ingredients until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap in plastic and rest at room temperature 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, make the filling: combine the ricotta, ham, mozzarella, parmesan, egg yolk, nutmeg, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Mix well and refrigerate until ready to use.
Roll the dough out thin (about 2mm), working in batches and keeping the rest covered.
Using a round cutter or a sorrentinos press (about 7cm), cut circles. Place a small spoonful of filling in the center of half the circles.
Top with a second circle, pressing out any air and sealing the edges firmly. Crimp with a fork.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the sorrentinos in batches 3-5 minutes, until they float and the pasta is tender.
Meanwhile, warm the tomato sauce with the butter in a pan.
Drain the sorrentinos, toss gently with the sauce, and serve with grated parmesan.

recipes.title: Pastel de Papa
recipes.dish_alt: A golden-topped slice of Pastel de Papa on a plate, with mashed potato browned on top
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Fork-Ridged Topping, Ready to Bake
recipes.prep_alt: An unbaked tray of Pastel de Papa with fork-ridged mashed potato topping

sections.heading: Mashed Potato Topping — Ingredients by Serving
Steps
items: Boil the potato in salted water until fork-tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and mash with the butter and milk until smooth. Season with salt.
Meanwhile, heat a little oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper (if using) 5 minutes until soft.
Add the ground beef, breaking it up, and cook until browned.
Stir in the paprika, cumin, and stock, simmering 3-4 minutes until slightly thickened. Season with salt.
Off the heat, stir in the raisins and olives.
Preheat the oven to 200°C/400°F. Spread half the mashed potato in the bottom of a baking dish. Layer the beef filling over it, then arrange the sliced hard-boiled egg on top.
Cover with the remaining mashed potato, smoothing the top with a fork to create ridges (this helps it brown). Sprinkle with cheese if using.
Bake 20-25 minutes until the top is golden brown, finishing under the broiler for the last 2-3 minutes for more color.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Guiso de Lentejas
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of thick Argentine lentil stew with chorizo, served with bread and lime
recipes.prep_alt: A pot of lentil stew simmering with visible lentils, carrots, and meat, being stirred with a wooden spoon

sections.heading: Steps
items: Heat a little oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chorizo and cook 2-3 minutes until it releases its fat and starts to brown.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and carrot, cooking 6-8 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and paprika, cooking 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato purée and cook 1-2 minutes.
Add the lentils, potato, bay leaf, and stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, partially covered, 30-35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and the stew has thickened.
Season with salt and pepper. Remove the bay leaf.
Serve hot with crusty bread.

recipes.title: Alfajores de Maicena (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: A whole coconut-rolled alfajor de maicena on a plate beside a cup of coffee
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Halved to Show the Dulce de Leche Filling
recipes.prep_alt: A chocolate-coated alfajor cut in half, revealing layered dulce de leche filling

sections.heading: Steps
items: Beat the butter and sugar together until light and creamy. Add the egg yolk(s) and vanilla, beating until smooth.
Sift in the cornstarch, flour, and baking powder. Fold in with a spatula, then bring together into a smooth, soft dough with your hands.
Wrap and chill 30-60 minutes until firm enough to roll.
Preheat the oven to 180°C/350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Roll the dough to about 6mm thick and cut into small rounds (about 4cm). Place on the baking sheet.
Bake 8-10 minutes - they should stay pale; don't let them brown. Cool completely on the tray (they're fragile while warm).
Sandwich pairs of cookies together with a generous spoonful of dulce de leche.
Roll the exposed dulce de leche edge in shredded coconut. Serve at room temperature; keeps in an airtight container for several days.
